findings.description:
Unverified variant of sarif-8fbfc6dbb67477650d1c8f305e9da7608d1e3ef3fafd034142d2a8b3d4c2ca79-526ff360b63f93e7b3b23e9c: Any signed-in user can read any tenant's invoice by id. GET /api/invoices/:id returned any tenant's invoice to any signed-in user because the route loaded the record with the unscoped invoiceRepo.findById(id) and never compared its orgId with the caller's. The fix scoped the lookup to the caller's o (hunt candidate C38)

A search thread reported this site from the same root cause. Nobody has confirmed it. Run `findings verify` on it to confirm or reject it.

Variant of the cross-tenant record authorization flaw: shipmentCostReport passes its shipmentId argument directly to shipmentRepo.get and returns financial shipment fields without validating that the shipment belongs to the requesting tenant. The listed caller is GET /shipments/:id/costs.

Suggested fix: Pass the authenticated orgId into shipmentCostReport and load with shipmentRepo.getForOrg(orgId, shipmentId), matching shipmentTimeline's tenant-scoped lookup.

findings.description:

GET /api/invoices/:id returned any tenant's invoice to any signed-in user because the route loaded the record with the unscoped invoiceRepo.findById(id) and never compared its orgId with the caller's. The fix scoped the lookup to the caller's o (hunt candidate C3)

A search thread reported this site from the same root cause. Nobody has confirmed it, so its severity is capped at medium (the thread said high). Run `findings verify` on it to confirm or reject it.

The webhook obtains `invoiceId` from the request body, resolves an integration account, then loads the invoice by global ID and marks it paid. No relationship between the account's organization and the invoice is checked. The signature helper signs the timestamp, not the body, so the verified signature does not establish that the invoice ID is authorized for that account.

Suggested fix: Resolve the invoice with the integration account's organization scope and reject mismatches; bind the delivered body to the webhook signature as well.

findings.title: Order import preview resolves products without tenant scoping
findings.description:
Unverified variant of sarif-8fbfc6dbb67477650d1c8f305e9da7608d1e3ef3fafd034142d2a8b3d4c2ca79-526ff360b63f93e7b3b23e9c: Any signed-in user can read any tenant's invoice by id. GET /api/invoices/:id returned any tenant's invoice to any signed-in user because the route loaded the record with the unscoped invoiceRepo.findById(id) and never compared its orgId with the caller's. The fix scoped the lookup to the caller's o (hunt candidate C10)

A search thread reported this site from the same root cause. Nobody has confirmed it. Run `findings verify` on it to confirm or reject it.

Variant: CSV product IDs reach `productRepo.findById` through `resolveProduct`; the returned product's name, unit price, and unit cost are included in the authenticated user's preview. No check restricts the product to the user's organization.

Suggested fix: Pass `user` into `resolveProduct` and use `productRepo.findForOrg(user.orgId, ref)`.

findings.title: GraphQL subscription resolver reads subscriptions without tenant scoping
findings.description:
Unverified variant of sarif-8fbfc6dbb67477650d1c8f305e9da7608d1e3ef3fafd034142d2a8b3d4c2ca79-526ff360b63f93e7b3b23e9c: Any signed-in user can read any tenant's invoice by id. GET /api/invoices/:id returned any tenant's invoice to any signed-in user because the route loaded the record with the unscoped invoiceRepo.findById(id) and never compared its orgId with the caller's. The fix scoped the lookup to the caller's o (hunt candidate C2)

A search thread reported this site from the same root cause. Nobody has confirmed it, so its severity is capped at medium (the thread said high). Run `findings verify` on it to confirm or reject it.

Variant: an authenticated user can provide a subscription ID to the GraphQL `subscription` resolver; it performs an unscoped lookup and returns the subscription. The route-level tenant-scoped lookup does not protect this separate resolver.

Suggested fix: Use `subscriptionRepo.findForOrg(ctx.user.orgId, String(args.id))` in this resolver.
